cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel, written for the choirmaster to the tune of "The Doe of the Dawn." The only tune in MY bakery is the oven timer, and friend, it knows ONE note. Then David opens his mouth: "My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?"

cards.question: In his opening cry, David says God feels so far away. So far from doing what for him?

cards.text: Friend, you might know that line. Jesus cried it out from the cross (Matthew 27:46).

cards.question: True or false: David says he cries out to God by day and by night, and God answers him right away.

cards.text: Then David says, "Yet You are holy, enthroned on the praises of Israel." And he remembers Israel's fathers, the ones who trusted God.

cards.question: When Israel's fathers trusted God, He ___ them.

cards.text: Then David says, "But I am a worm and not a man, scorned by men and despised by the people." Friend, I spent YEARS under the dust in a junk drawer, and I never once called myself a worm.

cards.question: The people who see David mock his trust in the LORD. They sneer that the LORD should ___ him.

cards.text: But David turns back to God with another "Yet." "Yet You brought me forth from the womb; You made me secure at my mother’s breast."

cards.question: True or false: David says God has been his God only since he became king.
David pleads with God not to be far from him. What reason does he give?

answers.text: Trouble is near and no one can help
He wants to see a sign from heaven
His enemies have all run away

cards.text: Now David paints his enemies as wild animals. Strong bulls of Bashan encircle him, and they open their jaws like lions that roar and maul.

cards.question: David says he is poured out like water and his heart melts like wax. What is he describing?

cards.text: His strength is dried up like a potsherd, and his tongue sticks to the roof of his mouth. Then he tells God, "You lay me in the dust of death."
And it gets darker. Dogs surround him, a band of evil men encircles him, and "they have pierced my hands and feet."

cards.question: True or false: David says he can count all his bones.
The men around David stare and gloat. What do they do with his clothing?

cards.text: Hold on, friend. John says the soldiers at Jesus' cross divided His clothes and cast lots, to fulfill this very Scripture (John 19:23-24).
Then David calls out one more time. "But You, O LORD, be not far off; O my Strength, come quickly to help me."

cards.question: David begs God to deliver him from the sword and from the power of wild dogs. What is he asking God to save?

cards.text: David asks God to save him from the mouth of the lion. Then he mentions the horns of the wild oxen.

cards.question: Right there at the horns of the wild oxen, what does David say God has done?
Now that God has answered, David says he will ___ God's name to his brothers.
True or false: David calls only the priests to praise the LORD.

cards.text: David calls everyone who fears the LORD, all of Jacob's descendants, to praise Him. And he tells them why.

cards.question: David gives Israel a reason to praise the LORD. What has the LORD done for the afflicted one?

cards.text: His praise resounds in the great assembly, and he'll fulfill his vows before those who fear God. Friend, he went from "I am a worm" to the great assembly, and THAT is a comeback.

cards.question: David says the ___ will eat and be satisfied.

cards.text: Then the picture gets BIG. All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the LORD, and all the families of the nations will bow down before Him.

cards.question: True or false: David says the nations will bow before the LORD because He rules over them.
True or false: David says the rich of the earth are left out of the worship.

cards.text: Even all who go down to the dust will kneel before Him, even those unable to preserve their lives.

cards.question: As the psalm ends, future generations will declare the Lord to a new generation. What will they proclaim about Him?

cards.text: They will proclaim His righteousness "to a people yet unborn—all that He has done." A psalm that started in the dark ends on all that God has done.

findings.problem: The card says David is king of Israel. That fact comes from outside Psalm 22, but the card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The joke 'I spent YEARS under the dust in a junk drawer, and I never once called myself a worm' sets Papa Dorin above David. It makes David's cry look overdramatic, so it laughs at the psalmist in his anguish instead of laughing at Papa Dorin himself. This is a line the New Testament ties to the crucifixion.

rule.text: Humble. When a joke needs someone to laugh at, it's himself. Humor about people in Bible stories laughs with their human situation, never at them.

findings.problem: 'Now David paints his enemies as wild animals' adds a label the text doesn't use. Psalm 22:12-13 speaks only of bulls and lions. It never calls them David's enemies or says who they stand for.

rule.text: Reasons. He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why. For example, Jonah 4:2 says why Jonah fled. It never calls Nineveh Jonah's enemies, so neither does he.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'His strength is gone', comes from Psalm 22:15 ('My strength is dried up'). Psalm 22:14 never mentions strength, yet the card cites only 22:14.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower. A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Tear it apart' is close to what the same verse says: 'They divide my garments among them.' A baker could argue it's right, and the dividing of the garments is true in the passage.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Card 6 has already asked who David calls to praise the LORD in Psalm 22:23. Card 7 then retells the answer to that question (everyone who fears the LORD, all of Jacob's descendants). The 22:23 story card should come before the choice card, not repeat it afterward.
